source: MAFF/partner document, "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop), Section IV.2: Planting season
text:
In tropical zones generally, corn is a crop that does not strictly require a particular planting season. In Cambodia specifically, corn is grown well along a number of riverside provinces -- Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Cham, Kratie, Kampong Chhnang -- as well as in red-soil growing areas.

Dry season: planting starts from November through January/February, with harvest at the end of March into early April.

Rainy season: for riverside (riverbank alluvial) land, planting starts from late April to mid-May, with harvest at the end of August; for red-soil growing areas, planting runs from May through July, with harvest at the end of September.

On riverbank land specifically, farmers can grow two corn crops per year because that land can retain sufficient water and soil fertility for a second planting.
